title: The path model of the homotopy coherent limit of a tower of spaces
statement: Use simplicial sets, internal functor simplicial sets and constant diagrams from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the endpoint map $e:P^{\Delta^1}\to P\times P$ from [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. For any sequence of simplicial sets $X_n$ and maps $p_n:X_{n+1}\to X_n$, put $P=\prod_{n\geq0}X_n$ and define the shift $s:P\to P$ by $\pi_ns= p_n\pi_{n+1}$. Define its path-model tower homotopy limit to be $H(X,p)=P\times_{P\times P}P^{\Delta^1}$, where $P\to P\times P$ is $(\mathrm{id},s)$ and the other map is $e$. If the $X_n$ are Kan complexes this is the path-space model for their homotopy coherent inverse limit: its simplices retain the paths from $x_n$ to $p_n(x_{n+1})$ and all their higher parameters. A strict cone $f_n:A\to X_n$ with $p_nf_{n+1}=f_n$ has the canonical comparison $A\to H(X,p)$ given by $(f_n)_n$ and its constant path. A strict map of towers $g_n:X_n\to Y_n$, $g_np_n=q_ng_{n+1}$, induces $H(X,p)\to H(Y,q)$ by the product map on sequences and postcomposition on paths. These maps are the actual pullback lifts of the displayed data; their endpoint-square equalities are the structural well-definedness laws of this construction.

source.place: Bill Dwyer, Homotopy theory and classifying spaces, Copenhagen June 2008, Exercise 6.23 and following homotopy-equalizer formula, printed p. 64. This is the explicit path model for the coherent inverse limit in HTT 5.3.4.11 and 5.3.4.13(6).
